role: Auditable bibliography for map and event dataset, with independent government/scholarly source distinction.

records.title: Neil Murphy (2019), The Tudor Occupation of Boulogne: Conquest, Colonisation and Imperial Monarchy, 1544–1550
records.finding: 1544 English conquest and settlement, forts and fiscal/border politics; until 1550
records.precision_warning: The monograph's paywalled full text and full historic map not inspected.

records.title: Murphy, Chapter 3, Conquest, Cartography and Treaty
records.finding: Land conquest/1546 peace and mapmaking to justify 1544–50 Boulogne annexation. Linear boundary maps historic but not accessed.
records.precision_warning: No source supports drawing exact Boulogne region boundary from abstract alone.

records.title: Murphy, Chapter 4, The Settlement of the Boulonnais
records.finding: English commissions redistributed farms, changed laws and religion, administered French peasant workforce.
records.precision_warning: Dates of each farm/occupied parish and precise geography not read; never count approximate polygon as measured estate.

records.title: Murphy, Chapter 5, The Boulogne Garrison
records.finding: English garrisons and fortified settlement, state fiscal burden.
records.precision_warning: Abstract does not contain detailed expenditure series or site-specific dates.

records.title: Murphy, Chapter 6, Tudor Occupation of Boulogne and English Imperialism
records.finding: Compares northern French military colonial settlement with English Ireland and Scottish warfare.
records.precision_warning: Cannot infer every geography/control point described in whole chapter.

records.title: The Battle of Pinkie, Mary Queen of Scots and the Anglo-Scottish Wars of the 1540s
records.finding: Documents 1547 Pinkie, English occupation of Broughty and Inchcolm, Scotland-France alliance and English fort attempts.
records.precision_warning: Contemporary 16c fortification survey maps not digitized.

records.title: The Story of Scotland's Longest Siege
records.finding: English occupation/Haddington fort in 1548 and prolonged Franco-Scottish siege through withdrawal 1549.
records.precision_warning: City historic military walls not georeferenced here.

records.title: Broughty Castle history and stories
records.finding: English captured Broughty Castle 1547 and maintained for two-and-half years, Scottish/French retook 1550.
records.precision_warning: Modern castle monument incorporates major 1860s rebuild; never draw visible present walls as 1547 perimeter.

records.title: Tudor Warships Ahoy! Inchcolm English garrison
records.finding: English force used Inchcolm 1547; withdrew in March 1548 due naval pressure; French then took Inchkeith, not Inchcolm.
records.precision_warning: Distinguish island abbey castle geography vs naval area; precise arrival month uncertain.

records.title: Crown of Ireland Act (Ireland), designated 1542 c. 1
records.institution: UK Legislation reference in Crime and Disorder Act 1998
records.finding: Modern British legislation explicitly cites 1542 c.1 Crown of Ireland Act; commonly described as 1541 Dublin Parliament act.
records.precision_warning: 1541 parliamentary passage versus official act short-title 1542 must be recorded separately. It changed royal style/claim, not effective control of Gaelic Ireland.

records.title: Tax grant 1545, military benevolence to finance Boulogne
records.institution: The National Archives E179 document notes
records.finding: Jan 1545 commissioners to raise military funds. Source quotes secondary estimate receipts £119,581 and identifies enrolled account E370/2/23, county returns E179.
records.precision_warning: £119,581 is historian's estimated realized collection, NOT Boulogne profit and not direct cost. Needs original roll for exact totals.

records.title: 1546 free and voluntary contribution for defending Boulogne/Calais
records.institution: The National Archives E179 document notes
records.finding: 16 May 1546 commissioners collected further grants to finance war in French enclaves.
records.precision_warning: No verified received total extracted; not colonial net gain.

records.title: Edward VI answers Western rebels: war expenses in Boulogne and Scotland
records.finding: 1549 royal reply explicitly admits Boulogne and Scottish garrison military costs and quotes inherited debt above £300,000.
records.precision_warning: Rhetorical royal text is a contemporary claim, not audited contemporary exchequer total; recorded debt is not profit.

records.title: Haddington siege heritage account: Hailes Castle and Forthill English fort
records.finding: English seized Hailes Castle March 1548, handed to Hugh Douglas, garrisoned by fifty English troops during Haddington siege; Tudor castle fort at nearby Forthill after 1547 Broughty seizure.
records.precision_warning: Hailes garrison end date must be researched; lordly local grant not territorial annexation of entire East Lothian.

records.title: Lochmaben Castle: history and stories — 1544 capture and 1545 Scots recovery
records.finding: Official historical account explicitly records castle taken by English forces in 1544 during Rough Wooing and recovered by Scots the next year (1545). Earlier 1385 Scottish recovery not the relevant episode.
records.precision_warning: Only castle change of hands, no date to month/day and no newly annexed Dumfriesshire region.

records.title: Lochmaben Castle, NRHE 66315
records.finding: Modern heritage castle record locates Lochmaben Castle at 55.11633 latitude, -3.43092 longitude; grid NY 0883 8115.
records.precision_warning: Modern stone ruins are not original 1544 occupation wall surveyed contour. Distinct from nearby Old Castle site NRHE 66314.

records.title: Dunglass designed landscape GDL00154 and the English encampment of 1548–49
records.institution: Historic Environment Scotland Trove / national designation
records.finding: Official designation reports an English encampment with ramparts and deep trenches on hill west of Dunglass House, used during English occupation Haddington 1548–49 and destroyed shortly afterward by Scots. Modern Dunglass estate point 55.93584, -2.38613, grid NT75976 71487.
records.read_scope: official full designation setting and site history
records.precision_warning: Coordinate is CURRENT Dunglass designated landscape anchor, not exactly hill camp or 1548 perimeter. Dunglass East Lothian, NOT separate Dunglass Castle in West Dunbartonshire. The date of dismantling is only 'shortly after', no exact 1549/1550 exit date.

records.title: Pierre Héliot, Les fortifications de Boulogne sous l'occupation anglaise (1544–1550)
records.finding: Uses Tudor royal dispatches and fortification reports; Boulogne surrender 13 Sep 1544; engineer John Rogers supervised Tudor English Ambleteuse citadel (began April 1546) and Mont Lambert/Boulemberg fort (began May 1546). Upon French advances 1549, Ambleteuse fell and English Boulemberg garrison withdrew; town Boulogne still held by England to 1550.
records.read_scope: Open indexed article passages and page-extracts accessible from Persée; NOT a line-by-line review of all 34 pages.
records.precision_warning: The article's schematic fortification plans are secondary diagrams, not licensed georeferenced Tudor administrative surveys. Do not trace polygons as actual 1546 walls without archaeological/map crosscheck.

records.title: Parcours Patrimonial : Histoire d’Ambleteuse
records.finding: English camp at Slack 1544, English fortified Ambleteuse subsequently; Henry II besieged English Slack fort on 24 August 1549 and captured English citadel in Ambleteuse 25 August 1549; English garrison retreated to Calais. Describes multiple 16th c English forts and 17th c Vauban structure separately.
records.read_scope: Official municipal history full visible text
records.precision_warning: 1544 camp must not be confused with 1546 building of main English citadel; modern Vauban fort built circa 1680 is NOT sixteenth-century English fort. Municipality text not authoritative measured perimeter of fort.

records.title: View of Boulogne, 1549, RCIN 721017
records.institution: Royal Collection Trust, historical military maps
records.finding: Public royal collection catalogue depicts British heraldic standards, English Boulogne defenses, French forts to south of river Liane, and possible English Boulemberg/Mont Lambert exterior fort begun 1546.
records.read_scope: Catalogue expert contextual description; the 1549 image itself has NOT been geo-registered or linework extracted.
records.precision_warning: Artistic print/schematic view, not a measured 1549 survey; do not digitize/redistribute original royal collection image without license. Use only to confirm relationships and geographic research questions.

records.title: Ambleteuse commune contemporary centroid (modern coordinates)
records.institution: Modern French commune gazetteer as summarized in reference entries
records.finding: Modern Ambleteuse locality center latitude 50.8102778 longitude 1.6072222, north of Boulogne.
records.precision_warning: Town center reference ONLY; not the English 1546 citadel/Slack fort/Chateau/Fort Rouge historical footprint. Vauban fort coordinates are different and must NOT be used to depict English Tudor fort.

records.title: Mont Lambert modern geographic hamlet reference
records.finding: Mont Lambert hamlet contemporary point latitude about 50.71777 longitude 1.65893; eastern heights outside occupied Boulogne city core.
records.read_scope: Indexed modern place metadata from pre-existing 1530s research
records.precision_warning: Hamlet centroid not guaranteed site of 1546 English fort Boulemberg, and historic fort wall perimeter unmeasured. Mark point location APPROXIMATE.

records.title: Hume Castle Preservation Trust – castle history of 1547 English surrender and 1548 Scottish recapture
records.finding: 1547-09-22 Hume Castle forced surrender after English Pinkie campaign with Lord Home heir hostage; English governor Edward Sutton, trust reports £700 spent on defense; 1548-12 Scots under 5th Lord Home recaptured castle and killed garrison except Sutton.
records.read_scope: full trust historical account read; no Tudor original paybook seen
records.precision_warning: £700 amount is LOCAL TRUST secondary statement NOT audited Exchequer spending; site walls rebuilt in eighteenth century, no Tudor polygon

records.title: Hume Castle medieval/modern site official location
records.finding: Hume Castle centroid lat 55.66515 lon -2.47093 OS grid NT70473 41394.
records.precision_warning: This is the visible castle site, but 1794 artificial battlements and walls are NOT verified 1547 military perimeter

records.title: Hume Castle scheduled monument SM387 and associated deserted settlement
records.finding: Medieval Scottish Border castle monument scheduled, late eighteenth-century rebuilt eye-catcher, HES says much current masonry later. Place retained independent Scottish sovereignty except English local 1547-48 garrison.
records.precision_warning: Modern protected area includes associated settlement; cannot adopt as historic English-conquered tract.

records.title: Pierre Héliot 1958 pp.10–35, detailed English and French forts around Boulogne
records.institution: Revue du Nord / Persée open scholarly page scan
records.finding: Describes English fortified Tour d'Odre from November 1544 (earthworks completed 1545 or early 1546), Young Man/Fort Rouge attested 17 July 1545, 1546 English Clements Bulwark at lower-town port and citadel, French-built opposing Outreau fort in July 1545. Lists English measured military plans c1545,1547,1549; no original GIS.
records.read_scope: Open Persée scholarly page text excerpts; source manuscript cartography has not been examined or licensed for tracing
records.precision_warning: French fort at Outreau MUST NOT be colored English. Héliot location descriptions are period qualitative and maps schematic, no exact polygon reproduced.

records.title: Pierre Héliot 1958, French siege fortification of Outreau opposite English Boulogne
records.finding: French army under François I took Outreau heights 1545, began fort around July 1545; strategically opposed English Boulogne, with fortifications added through 1548. Not an English fort.
records.read_scope: Read scholarly full-text snippets and page scans
records.precision_warning: Modern town Outreau is not exact French fort; avoid putting English control color or treating whole modern Outreau as fortress.

records.title: Tour d’Ordre former Roman lighthouse and English Tudor fort location
records.institution: Wikidata Q3533260, source French Wikipedia for modern reconstruction
records.finding: Recorded location 50°43′54″ N 1°35′50″ E (~50.7316667,1.5972222) for former Tour d'Ordre; local heritage source identifies historical lighthouse/foundations cliff.
records.read_scope: Wikidata coordinate reference metadata read, Héliot historic fort corroboration
records.precision_warning: Geo is secondary approximation and former lighthouse on eroding cliff; Tudor earthwork actual footprint unknown, no ancient building outline.

records.title: BnF RAMEAU authority Boulonnais 1544–1550 English occupation and treaty
records.finding: BnF authority text: 24 March 1550 Treaty of Capécure/Outreau/Boulogne returns Boulogne and Boulonnais to France for 400,000 gold écus; 1546 Ardres settlement includes French debt annuities 250,000 livres; terms are not realized audited net colonial profits.
records.read_scope: French National Library authority chronology read; not original 1550 treaty manuscript
records.precision_warning: Treaty year 1550, NOT to be backdated as 1549 territory loss. 400k gold ecus is treaty price and not Boulogne 1540s extracted fiscal revenue.

records.title: Forthill English fort 1548–1550 separate from Broughty Castle
records.institution: National Library of Scotland digital historical Ordnance Gazetteer of Scotland
records.finding: Forthill hill in Monifieth parish about half mile NW Broughty Castle; English constructed fort in 1548 as supporting artillery position, dismantled 1550; original trace erased by 1782.
records.precision_warning: Named Forthill 1548 English fort is historical source not Tudor original; exact hilltop modern WGS84 cannot be safely derived from a half-mile description. Avoid invented polygon or precise pin.

records.title: Ruines mariales et boulevards anglais à Boulogne aux XVIe et XVIIe siècles
records.institution: Institut de recherches historiques du Septentrion, OpenEdition Books
records.finding: OpenEdition study of English 1540s Boulogne urban fortification including Clements Bulwark on lower-town harbor; historical maps depict building positions but not verified modern georectification.
records.read_scope: Scholarly abstract and illustrative historical maps, original image license not confirmed
records.precision_warning: Do not reproduce / trace historic colored maps without source-specific rights clearance; old port shoreline different.

records.title: Murphy 2019 Ch3 Tudor territorial surveying and the 1546 peace
records.finding: Henry VIII deployed geometric cartography to assert linear territorial borders of conquered Boulogne in 1540s; historically meaningful measured plans exist and remain to georeference.
records.read_scope: Full academic publisher chapter abstract read, full chapter not accessed
records.precision_warning: Existence of Tudor cartography does not authorize invented polygons on modern maps.

records.title: Forthill contemporary Dundee locality anchor (not Tudor fort walls)
records.finding: Modern Forthill quarter at 56.47487,-2.87601; historical 1548 English fort is said half mile NW of Broughty Castle but exact actual building site vanished.
records.precision_warning: Use only dashed/uncertain hill neighborhood marker; don't pretend a 1548 exact trace.

records.title: Outreau commune contemporary centroid, Pas-de-Calais
records.finding: Town centroid approx 50.704444,1.594722; French siege fort on Outreau HILL, exact 1545 position not determined by modern town center.
records.precision_warning: French Outreau fort not English-held; town center NOT hill fort exact site, suggest research event point only.

records.title: Héliot 1958: 1546 English expulsion and lower-town expropriations in Boulogne
records.institution: Revue du Nord on Persée historical source analysis
records.finding: English Boulogne garrison councillors in 1546 considered removing remaining foreign civilian inhabitants; Privy Council said city population should not exceed 5000, and citadel lower-town construction displaced local householders including Cordeliers friars. Distinguish population CAP ordered from observed inhabitants, and dispossession from quantified colony profit.
records.read_scope: scholarly article pp 23–26 text on Persée read
records.precision_warning: 5000 is Tudor administrative policy target, NOT verified deportees number; households expropriated not enumerated; avoid fabricated totals.
